notes: The accept twin of reject-existing-sleep-helper-newly-called: instead of a new call to the fixed sleep helper sleepQuietly(), the patch adds a call to the test class's existing private helper quiesce(). quiesce() drains the dispatcher board in a loop that rechecks on every pass whether the board and the pending reads stayed idle, is bounded by a deadline of QUIESCE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (10 s), calls sleepQuietly() between passes, and throws IllegalStateException when the deadline passes without the condition holding. ADR 0007 Decision 7 judges such a hand written poll loop as a condition wait, and newly calling an existing helper built this way is allowed on the same terms; the sleep inside it is a poll interval. The catch in sleepQuietly is the allowed InterruptedException idiom. Adapted: built on the post image of the commit that created the test (apache/pulsar PR 26174), as its twin is; the one added line is hand written and repeats the quiesce() call on the line before it, so the change is the smallest one that newly reaches the helper.
